title: Necessary bound for hypercontractivity
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\mu$, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$, let $r$ be a positive integer, and let $\rho\in\mathbb{R}$. Suppose $\mathbb{E}_{\mu}[X^2]=1$, every odd moment $\mathbb{E}_{\mu}[X^{2j-1}]$ vanishes for $1\le j\le r$, and for all $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$ the $2r$-norm of $a+\rho bX$ is at most the $2$-norm of $a+bX$. Then $\rho^2\le 1/(2r-1)$.
hypotheses_covered: Finite probability space and probability mass function
Odd moments vanish for every integer j with 1 ≤ j ≤ r
For all real a,b, the stated 2r-norm is at most the stated 2-norm
